summary.intent: Plan and execute Phase 49 of CipherBox (shared-folder intra-share move + useFolderNavigation consolidation + batch/drag parity), then run full PR-QA (simplify, two security reviews, CodeRabbit CLI/GitHub, push + PR, resolve review comments). A CI failure in the subsequent e2e run uncovered a missing write-key distribution for descendant shared subfolders, which cascaded into a fundamental architectural decision to decentralize the IPNS cache from per-user to per-name keying with signature-based authorization.
summary.outcome: PR #509 was created and all pre-push QA passed (SDK 235/web 54 unit tests, tsc+lint clean, CodeRabbit CLI + GitHub review fully resolved). CI-e2e revealed two regressions (SelectionActionBar layout-shift breaking dblclick navigation; spec folder-name mismatch with trailing slash) which were fixed and re-run. A third CI failure exposed that write shares never distributed `folder-ipns`/`file-ipns` keys for descendants, leading to a two-part fix: (1) client-side write-key distribution committed, and (2) IPNS cache re-architecture (per-name keying + Ed25519 signature verification + anti-rollback check) implemented and tested but not yet committed at session end.

repo: Private vault's SelectionActionBar gates on `selectedIds.size > 1`, not `> 0` — critical for dblclick navigation because a single click (the first half of a dblclick) on size > 0 causes a layout shift that moves the row off the click coordinate before the second click fires.
SharedFolderRow renders folder names with a decorative trailing `/` — page-object `getFolderItemNames()` must strip it; other specs already use slash-tolerant `.includes()` for this reason.

`collectChildKeys` (key-wrapping.ts) has always emitted only `'folder'`/`'file'` (read) keys for descendants, never `folder-ipns`/`file-ipns` write keys — so every owner-created subfolder/file in a write share was read-only to the recipient.

CipherBox's IPNS cache (`folder_ipns` entity) was keyed `@Unique(['userId','ipnsName'])` with `findActiveWriteShare` as the sole server-side publish authorization for non-owners. The TEE republishes the owner's enrolled rows every 6h, which overwrites any non-owner DHT update — making server-side authz unavoidable under the old model.

The `ipns` package's `validate(pubKey, marshalledRecord)` verifies Ed25519 SignatureV2 records and is already transitively available in `@cipherbox/crypto` — so server-side signature verification was always feasible.

`CHILD_KEY_TYPES` array in `apps/api/src/shares/types.ts` drives both `@IsIn` validation and `@ApiProperty enum` on `ChildKeyDto` — adding an entry there propagates automatically to both validation and the regenerated API client.
API migrations are glob-loaded from the migrations directory; adding a file is sufficient for registration.

SDK `dist/` is gitignored (CI rebuilds it), but must be rebuilt locally after public API additions — web's `tsc -b` checks the built dist, not source. New public methods appear in `client.d.ts`, not `index.d.ts` (the barrel re-export).
Web package has no `typecheck` script; use `pnpm --filter @cipherbox/web exec tsc -b` instead.
CodeRabbit CHILL profile delivers nitpicks in the review body, not as inline threads — `resolve-pr-reviews` will correctly report 0 unresolved threads even when actionable feedback exists.

`ipnsName` is the public key in CIDv1 encoding — key-possession alone is insufficient for server authorization because any authenticated user could replay a validly-signed record from the DHT to roll back another user's folder, necessitating an anti-rollback sequence check.
CodeRabbit CLI (`--agent` flag) produces structured JSON findings with fields `{severity, fileName, codegenInstructions, suggestions}` — not the flat text format.

code.finding: Private vault gates SelectionActionBar on `selectedIds.size > 1` — the model the shared browser should mirror to avoid layout-shift on single click (first half of dblclick).

`findActiveWriteShare` was the only server-side publish authorization for non-owner IPNS updates — an exact ipnsName match against a top-level write Share row, covering only the share root, not descendants.
When no existing row is found for `(userId, ipnsName)`, `upsertFolderIpns` forks a new user-owned record — causing a duplicate for the same ipnsName under the old per-user schema.

DB-first publish pattern: the server writes the signed record to `folder_ipns` synchronously before fire-and-forgetting to the DHT. Resolution always prefers the DB row, making the DB the true source of truth for IPNS resolution.
`resolveRecord` queries `findOne({ where: { ipnsName } })` with no user filter — already correct/decentralized, but non-deterministic when duplicate rows exist under the old schema.

`collectChildKeys` hard-codes `'folder'`/`'file'` key types — no permission param, never emits `folder-ipns`/`file-ipns`. Fixed to accept a `permission` param and emit write keys for descendants on write shares, guarding `file-ipns` on the optional `FilePointer.ipnsPrivateKeyEncrypted` field.

`enumerateSharedSubtree` writability check requires a per-subfolder `share_keys` row with `keyType: 'folder-ipns'` — previously never emitted for descendants, so every owner-created subfolder appeared read-only in the move dialog.
`CHILD_KEY_TYPES` is the single source of truth for both DTO validation (`@IsIn`) and OpenAPI enum (`@ApiProperty`) — adding `'folder-ipns'` here propagates automatically to the regenerated client.

workflow: GSD sequential execution (no worktrees) is more reliable for AFK/autonomous runs — avoids the worktree merge-base footguns and cwd-drift issues that the parallel-worktree merge-back protocol is prone to.
Must rebuild SDK dist between execution waves whenever public API changes, before running web typecheck — the cross-package dist-staleness gotcha.
After a GSD plan-check catch + RESEARCH.md doc-formatting nits, re-running the checker passes only when both the doc fix AND the substantive gap are addressed in the same iteration.

CodeRabbit CLI review should run before PR creation; the GitHub-posted review comes after PR and may contain different/overlapping findings. CHILL profile won't auto-re-review incremental fix pushes, so confirming 'no new findings' requires manually checking the run or accepting silence as clean.

When CI reveals a regression that traces to a missing layer in the underlying architecture (write-key distribution → server IPNS authorization), the right call is to scope the architectural fix into the same PR rather than deferring — mid-PR rebases create more friction than the expanded scope.
`gh workflow run` can silently succeed despite a CLI-level timeout error — always verify dispatch with `gh run list` rather than trusting the exit code.

Disabling local commit signing (`git config --local commit.gpgsign false`) for AFK sessions is viable but requires a signed rebase before merge on repos with signature enforcement — worth explicitly noting in the PR description as a merge blocker.

friction: gsd-tools commit helper false-negatives: multiple executors reported `commit_failed` while commits actually landed — required manual `git log` verification after each executor.
Web package has no `typecheck` script, unlike SDK/e2e — the discovery that `pnpm --filter @cipherbox/web exec tsc -b` is the right incantation only came after trying `pnpm typecheck` variants.
JSX comment placed inside a `{cond && (...)}` single-child expression caused TS1005, requiring a fixup commit.

TS2352/TS2493 typing for vitest mock call arrays required `(c as unknown as [string, { itemId: string }])[1]` workaround — the straightforward cast `(c[1] as ...)` fails because the mock tuple is typed as `[]`.

CodeRabbit false-positive (finding 2: `expect(setError).not.toHaveBeenCalled()`) — `runWrite` calls `setError(null)` on entry to clear prior errors, which is correct but made the suggested assertion wrong. Reverted after a test failure.
Three pre-existing API tsc errors (unrelated to phase 49 changes) caused noise in typecheck output on every pass.
Intel API surface regeneration produced an empty file (regex extractor unpopulated) — not the real artifact, but caused a moment of confusion about whether the intel gate was satisfied.
Transient network timeout when re-dispatching `ci-e2e` workflow run via `gh workflow run` — dispatch landed despite CLI error, but required `gh run list` verification.
CodeRabbit CHILL profile doesn't auto-re-review incremental fix pushes — no automated confirmation that addressed findings were accepted.
The drag-routing critical bug (moves wrong items when some are selected) was only caught by CodeRabbit CLI, not by local unit tests or the simplify/security passes — requires e2e to observe.
open_items: Commits on the branch are unsigned (local gpgsign disabled for AFK session) — requires a signed rebase or admin override before the PR can merge (repo enforces signed commits).

Live e2e UAT: `shared-folder-move.spec.ts` is authored and type-checked but main-push-gated (needs docker stack with two accounts). The third CI failure (test 3.3) was the trigger for the write-key distribution work and was still unconfirmed green at session end.

IPNS architectural change (Commit B: per-name keying, signature-based authorization, anti-rollback sequence check, hand-rolled parser removal, migration) was fully implemented and tested (134 IPNS + 289 shares/republish/vault tests pass) but not yet committed or pushed at session end.

Full SDK-level descendant cycle guard (SDK refuses to move folder A into its own subtree) deferred — current protection is UI-only picker exclusion + SDK self-move throw. Documented in PR as proportionate residual (actor already holds write keys).
Batch move key-refetch performance: `batchMoveItemsHandler` re-fetches the share write key for each item individually — acceptable for v1 but noted as a follow-up optimization.
`useMultiSelect` extraction into a shared hook (for private + shared browser parity) deferred as cross-boundary scope creep beyond phase 49.
`enumerateSharedSubtree` DFS concurrency: currently sequential per-level — deferred due to gateway-rate-limit tradeoff, noted as follow-up.

Revocation semantics changed by the IPNS architectural shift: revoking a write share no longer prevents a key-holding recipient from publishing indefinitely — revocation now requires IPNS key rotation + re-share, which is a deliberate architectural tradeoff accepted by the user but not yet documented in any ADR or ROADMAP note.

The generated API client was regenerated as part of the `folder-ipns` ChildKeyDtoKeyType addition — the regeneration also included an OpenAPI spec-version bump (0.39.0→0.40.0) across all generated models, which was benign but not intentional.
